channel.title: GM Research
channel.description: Daily intelligence briefings on markets, law, AI, biohacking, trading and more.

item.title: Morning Edge: Nvidia beat fails to lift stocks as BTC slides below $64.5K and Fed hike bets firm
item.description: Yesterday's thesis reversed on price: Nvidia fell 2.9% after a record beat, BTC is near $63K, and December Fed hike odds sit near 88%.

item.title: Precedent: Fourth Circuit Rules States Can Target Kalshi’s Prediction-Market Event Contracts
item.description: The Fourth Circuit ruled on 17 November that states may target prediction-market event contracts, handing Kalshi its third federal appellate loss.

item.title: Cortex: Anthropic's ANT listing day arrives as Marvell agrees to a $115B Lumentum deal
item.description: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut today, the week's biggest deal (Marvell and Lumentum), decentralized AI token moves tied to IPO attention, and MCP becoming shared agent infrastructure.

item.title: Praxis: You cannot forecast the risk that hurts you, so design for the surprise instead
item.description: Housel's risk essays and Mollick's jagged-AI framing converge: when failure cannot be forecast, build margin and test by hand.

item.title: Alpha: Passive vs Aggressive Flow: which side of the book is absorbing the tape
item.description: Every trade pairs one aggressor with one resting order. Learn to read which side is winning at a level, using BTC's 18 Nov 2026 liquidation hours as the live example.

item.title: Rabbit Hole: Why about 30% of real numbers start with 1 — and how worn pages found the pattern
item.description: In 1881 an astronomer noticed his logarithm tables were worn at the front. The pattern became Benford's law, and today it flags fabricated data.

item.title: Morning Edge: Nvidia beats on record revenue; BTC holds $64.5K as a December Fed hike gets priced
item.description: Yesterday's BTC and Fed call held at $64.6K, but Nvidia's after-hours beat challenges its 52-week-low leg. Hike odds near 90%. Lean bearish into the 9 December FOMC.

item.title: Precedent: CFTC Grants Backpack Contract-Market and Clearing Approvals for US Perpetuals
item.description: Backpack won CFTC designated contract market status on 16 November, with its clearing affiliate already registered, opening a route to US-regulated perpetual contracts.

item.title: Cortex: Anthropic prices its Nasdaq IPO tonight; ANT trades from 19 November
item.description: The $70–$78 range is set to be finalised on the US evening of 18 November, with reported demand well above the offer. Also: Qwen4-Max pricing and Akash's Solana move.

item.title: Biohacker: Five lifespan treatments converge on ergothioneine in mice — human data still absent
item.description: Frontiers in Aging maps shared metabolite shifts across five longevity interventions. Training volume and a CoQ10 RCT add practical limits for Tony's PPL block.

item.title: Alpha: Orderbook Depth & Spread: a tight quote can sit on a thin book
item.description: Spread prices your first unit, depth prices the rest. BTC's mid-November sell-off showed how a thin book lets a market order walk far from mid.

item.title: Rabbit Hole: The tar that shatters like glass is a liquid, and it has been dripping since 1930
item.description: Parnell's 1927 funnel: nine drops in about 90 years, a viscosity far above honey's, and a tenth drop that is still forming.

item.title: Morning Edge: BTC at $64.6K as Fed hike bets and ETF exits hold; Nvidia hits a 52-week low
item.description: Yesterday's thesis is playing out: BTC is below $68K, December hike odds sit near 90%, and Nvidia's slide into tonight's earnings is dragging the tape.

item.title: Precedent: Russia Opens Regulated Retail Crypto Trading Today Under a ₽300,000 Annual Cap
item.description: Bank of Russia rules let licensed exchanges and brokers offer bitcoin, ether and USDT to retail investors from 17 November, subject to annual purchase caps.

item.title: Cortex: Anthropic says Claude ported to AMD GPUs in three days as IPO pricing nears
item.description: Anthropic's IPO disclosure claims a three-day AMD GPU port; pricing is set for 18 November. Plus Qwen4-Max, a local 137.9B coder from Microsoft, and Bittensor's Tencent tie-in.

item.title: Praxis: Your spending follows the tribe you compare against, not the income you earn
item.description: Housel's essays and a Morningstar interview converge: your reference group sets your baseline, so name it before the next raise resets it.

item.title: Alpha: Stop Clusters & Magnet Zones: why price returns to the stops it can fill against
item.description: Stop-loss and breakout orders cluster beyond obvious highs and lows, and each touched stop becomes a market order. BTC's weekend sweep below $62,000 is the live case.

item.title: Rabbit Hole: The $125M Mars orbiter lost because one file said pounds, not newtons
item.description: A 1999 NASA spacecraft flew too low after a ground file reported thrust in the wrong unit, a 4.45× error that every internal check missed.

item.title: Morning Edge: BTC loses $68K and the 200-week line as Fed hike odds and ETF outflows bite
item.description: Yesterday's $68K breakout reversed: BTC near $65K after seven ETF outflow sessions, a near-certain December Fed hike and an Nvidia leadership shock.

item.title: Precedent: Louisiana AG Attacks CFTC Chair as Prediction-Market Fight Escalates
item.description: Louisiana’s attorney general publicly attacked the CFTC chair after the agency sued the state over prediction markets; the GENIUS Act rule clock keeps running.

item.title: Cortex: Anthropic sets $70–$78 IPO range; Nasdaq debut expected 19 Nov
item.description: 825M shares, up to about $64B raised at the top of the range, roughly $1.4T fully diluted. Plus Bittensor's early subnet revenue and Fractile's $720M chip raise.

item.title: Biohacker: Lean mass alone misreads metabolic risk: ectopic fat changes the link
item.description: A 59,269-person UK Biobank analysis finds visceral and intramuscular fat reshape the lean-mass and metabolic syndrome relationship. Volume beats frequency in new hypertrophy data.

item.title: Alpha: Spoofing & Iceberg Orders: fake size pulled, real size hidden
item.description: A spoof is size placed to be cancelled; an iceberg is real size shown in slices. Judge any resting order by what it does when price touches it.

item.title: Rabbit Hole: The Keyboard Built to Stop Jams, Not to Slow You Down — and the Myth That Stuck
item.description: QWERTY was never meant as a handicap on typists. The real fault was mechanical, and the layout survived because switching away would cost more than it saves.

item.title: Morning Edge: BTC breaks $68K and the 200-week line as Fed hike bets lift yields
item.description: Yesterday's $68K hold failed. BTC is near $63.4K with Fear & Greed at 13, seven days of ETF outflows and a near-certain December Fed hike.

item.title: Precedent: Louisiana Court Bars 31 Prediction-Market Entities as CFTC Sues the State
item.description: A Louisiana state order barring event contracts for 31 entities, including Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and Coinbase, drew a federal CFTC suit on 13 November.

item.title: Cortex: Anthropic's IPO price range firms up as Inkling 2 Small weights go open
item.description: Anthropic sets a $70 to $78 IPO range with pricing on 18 Nov. Thinking Machines opens the 594B Inkling 2 Small under Apache 2.0, and llama.cpp hits 1.0.

item.title: Praxis: AI can do expert work, but judging whether its output is good still falls to you
item.description: Mollick's jagged-AGI tests and Housel's case for a good bullshit detector converge: when output is cheap, the scarce skill is setting and applying the quality bar.

item.title: Alpha: Absorption: when heavy selling hits a level and price refuses to fall
item.description: Absorption is aggressive volume that fails to move price because passive size keeps refilling. How to read it on footprint, and the BTC long flush of 14 November.

item.title: Morning Edge: Nvidia CEO exit drags AI chips as BTC holds $68K in extreme fear
item.description: S&P 500 slipped Friday after a strong week, BTC is down 4.1% to about $68.3K and Fear & Greed sits at 13. Bearish lean into Nvidia's Tuesday print.

item.title: Precedent: CLARITY Act Stalls Past the Midterms With No Senate Vote Scheduled
item.description: Democrats' midterm sweep leaves the failed 49-50 Senate cloture vote unresolved, with no new vote set and only a lame-duck window before January 2027.

item.title: Cortex: Gemini 4 Hydrogen ships at flat long-context pricing as Anthropic firms up IPO terms
item.description: Google's Hydrogen model arrives at $1.50 and $7.50 per million tokens across a 1M window. Anthropic's IPO pricing date is set for 18 November, and Schwab opens its MCP server.

item.title: Biohacker: Low testosterone linked to 18% higher cancer death risk in 26,000 men
item.description: A Lancet Healthy Longevity cohort ties the lowest testosterone fifth to higher cancer mortality. Plus: 2026 training-volume evidence and a protein-restriction review.

item.title: Alpha: Sweep Orders: one market order that eats several price levels at once
item.description: A sweep consumes resting size across levels in one burst. Compare its size with the first level and watch the refill before trading the reaction.

item.title: Morning Edge: BTC slides to $68.5K as crypto flushes into extreme fear while equities rally
item.description: Crypto is deleveraging on its own: BTC -6.7%, ETH -6.0%, Fear & Greed 20, while the S&P 500 is up 3.2%. Bearish lean until a selling climax.

item.title: Precedent: Treasury Bars U.S. Banks From Moving Funds for MEXC Global Over $16.7bn in Illicit Flows
item.description: FinCEN's Section 9714 order cuts MEXC Global off from covered U.S. financial institutions, effective about 10 December 2026, after $16.7bn in linked transactions.

item.title: Cortex: Claude Fable 5.2 takes the top index spot as Anthropic's IPO roadshow opens
item.description: Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 shipped 9 Nov and lead the Artificial Analysis index at 65. Claude Meetings, Sheets and Whiteboards hit beta as the ANT roadshow began.

item.title: Praxis: Long-term choices fail because the person who pays for them feels like a stranger
item.description: Hershfield's future self-continuity research, Housel on inherited discipline, and a 2025 AI future-self study converge on one fix: make the beneficiary specific.

item.title: Alpha: Footprint Charts: the candle opened up to show who was aggressive at each price
item.description: Footprint charts split every candle into bid and ask volume at each price, so you can see who hit and who lifted. Read through the 13 Nov BTC flush.

item.title: Rabbit Hole: The Calm Cameroon Lake That Exhaled Death in 1986 — and the Pipe That Tamed It
item.description: A gas held under 208 metres of water, a small trigger, and a silent night: how Lake Nyos killed about 1,700 people, and why the fix is a pipe.
